name: InputOtp
description: One-time-password input: one hidden field drives a row of character slots, with separators, obscuring, validation and form participation.

fields.background: StateValue<ThemedColor>? - per-state slot fill; null = input@0.3 rest / 0.5 hovered
fields.borderColor: StateValue<ThemedColor>? - per-state slot border; null = input
fields.borderWidth: double? - used when borderColor resolves; null = 1
fields.textStyle: TextStyle? - its colour is ignored (taken from foreground)
fields.spacing: double? - gap between slots; null = the density base gap
fields.separatorTextStyle: TextStyle? - style of the optional separator
fields.cursorColor: ThemedColor? - caret of the focused slot; null = ring

notes: One hidden `EditableText` replaces the old per-slot `TextField` + `FocusNode` + `GlobalKey` design, so typing, paste, undo and the caret are the framework's.

`InputOTPChild`, `CharacterInputOTPChild`, `WidgetInputOTPChild`, `InputOTPChildData`, `OTPSeparator`, `CodepointPredicate`, `CodepointUnaryOperator` and `OTPCodepointList` are deleted: the whole factory DSL existed only to configure skeleton-style per-slot fields.
The value is a `String`, not `List<int?>` of UTF-16 code units: a surrogate pair (an emoji) used to occupy two slots.

The batch data lists `input` and `input_features` as dependencies; neither is imported, so `deps.components` is empty and `deps.primitives` has no `input_features` (an unimported dep would raise an `unused-dependency` finding).
`onChanged` is driven by the host's controller listener alone. Wiring both that and `EditableText.onChanged` reported every edit twice.
Filtering runs before truncating in `_clampCode`; the reverse order cut the code at the last *unfiltered* character and threw the valid ones behind it away.

The controller listener also fires for a selection-only change (focus selects offset 0), so the reported text is compared against the last one; otherwise `onChanged` fired with an empty code right after mounting.
